Disease Outbreak Disrupts Oil & Gas Services & Equip Operations in Mexico

A respiratory disease outbreak has hit Mexico’s Oil & Gas Services & Equipment industry, with at least 300 reported cases among workers at major field sites across Tabasco and Veracruz, industry representatives confirmed Wednesday. Several companies, including Grupo Enerflex and Servicios Petroleros Norte, have temporarily suspended operations at affected locations to contain the spread, halting ongoing drilling and maintenance projects.

“We are prioritizing the health and safety of our workforce,” said Laura Jiménez, spokesperson for Servicios Petroleros Norte. “Essential crews remain on site only for critical safety monitoring, while the majority of staff have been sent home or are under medical observation.”

The Mexican Association of Oilfield Service Providers reported that up to 40% of scheduled field work has been delayed since the outbreak was first identified last week. “We are working closely with health authorities to implement strict containment measures,” said association president Rodrigo Torres. “However, the impact on project timelines is already significant, with key well servicing and equipment installation activities postponed indefinitely at multiple sites.”

Analysts note the disruption is likely to affect near-term revenues for service providers, as well as worker availability. “The outbreak has forced firms to reconsider shift patterns, limit crew sizes, and introduce new sanitization protocols, all of which reduce operational efficiency,” said industry analyst Marisol Vega.

Union leaders have called for enhanced health protections, with Jesús Hernández of the National Oil Services Workers Union stating, “Our members deserve rigorous safeguards and clear communication as the situation evolves.”

As of this morning, no timeline has been set for full resumption of activities, with industry officials monitoring the situation daily.
